summary.title: Write Simply
summary.one_liner: Plain words and short sentences make readers engage more deeply and keep reading, and they're a sign of honest, careful writing.
takeaways: Ordinary words and simple sentences lower reading effort, so readers engage more and read further.
Fancy writing can hide a lack of ideas; simple writing exposes it to you and to readers.
Simple writing is more considerate and is also more likely to stay understandable over time.
Write a fast first draft, then edit heavily, mostly by cutting, to make prose simpler.
Use complex sentences or fancy words only on purpose, never by accident.
summary.summary: Paul Graham's short March 2021 essay argues that writers should use ordinary words and simple sentences. He gives several reasons: simple prose is easier to read and keeps readers going, it respects readers (including non-native English speakers), it exposes empty writing, and it lasts longer. His main stated reason is that fancy prose seems clumsy to him. He recommends writing a fast first draft and then editing, mostly by cutting, over several days.
